title: Cold rebuild: Find the flaky tests
summary: Rebuild Find the flaky tests from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Find the flaky tests** in *Flaky tests and quality gates*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: `OrderExpires_after_30_minutes` fails about once a week, always shortly after midnight UTC. What is the most likely cause?
options: It reads the real clock and a date boundary changes the result; inject a clock (`TimeProvider`) instead
The CI runner is too slow
The test needs to be retried three times
steps.explain: Tests that read `DateTime.Now` behave differently at boundaries. .NET 8's `TimeProvider` lets tests use a fake, fixed clock.
